articles.title_orig: Iran attacks US air base in Kuwait
articles.title_zh: Iran attacks US air base in Kuwait
articles.content_orig:
Iran targeted a Kuwaiti air base that hosts US forces on Wednesday, widening the scope of its attacks after the US military hit what it said was a missile launch site in Iran.
Iran’s army targeted Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait with drones, state-run Press TV reported. The Kuwaiti Army’s General Staff said any explosions heard were caused by air defense systems intercepting incoming attacks.
Neighboring Bahrain, which is home to the US Fifth Fleet and has faced repeated Iranian attacks over the past week, also sounded air raid sirens early Wednesday, with the military saying it had intercepted “a number of Iranian aerial attacks” early Wednesday.
CNN has contacted the US Central Command (CENTCOM) for comment.
Just hours earlier, US fighter jets carried out a “self-defense” strike against an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm Island using “precision munitions,” according to an American military official.
The strike “was in response to IRGC aggression targeting American personnel and assets,” the official said, noting that CENTCOM remains “highly vigilant and fully postured to protect Americans across the region.”
Iranian state media reported that an area on the outskirts of a city on Qeshm Island had been targeted in an “enemy attack.” Ahmad Nafisi, the deputy governor of Hormozgan province for political and security affairs, said the strike caused no damage to vital infrastructure, commercial or residential areas.
Iran’s widening attacks come as Tehran warns it will not accept a prolonged stalemate in its war with the US, while President Donald Trump has signaled a preference for maintaining crippling economic pressure on the Islamic Republic rather than resuming full-scale hostilities. Iran has also threatened to expand the war significantly and warned that it will not wait for another US attack before striking.
Tuesday’s US strikes appear similar to others in recent weeks around the Strait of Hormuz, which US officials have also characterized as defensive, rather than marking a significant escalation by American forces.
A third US aircraft carrier strike group recently entered CENTCOM’s area of responsibility, where it is expected to — at least temporarily — join ongoing operations that include enforcing a blockade of Iranian ports and conducting escort operations for commercial ships willing to transit the Strait.
Attacks on oil and gas tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz have surged in recent weeks. On Wednesday, the United Arab Emirates’ state-owned ADNOC energy company said one of its vessels had been attacked while transiting the waterway the previous evening, leaving 11 crew members injured and one missing.
“Today’s developments should serve as an important reminder of the inherent instability of the current situation,” Hamidreza Azizi, an Iran analyst at Crisis Group, wrote on X. “Some within the Trump administration – and perhaps even Trump himself – may believe that Washington can maintain economic pressure and the naval blockade against Iran indefinitely while avoiding another full-scale war. But the developments of the past 24 hours demonstrate how difficult it is to sustain such an arrangement.”
There is little indication of an imminent diplomatic agreement to end the conflict, and Trump has warned he could resume full combat operations if Tehran refuses to accept the US administration’s demands.
Trump was widely expected to hold off on restarting those combat operations until after the US midterm elections but appears to still be mulling over how to proceed, absent a last-minute deal.
With Democrats poised to take control of the House and Senate in January, Trump’s window to decide on a path forward in Iran appears to be shrinking. CNN has previously reported that it is likely untenable for the US military to maintain the status quo indefinitely, but only Trump has the power to decide when the war is over.
CNN’s Abbas Al Lawati, Lucas Lilieholm and Mohammed Tawfeeq contributed reporting.

articles.title_orig: Stocks Fall as Nvidia’s Earnings Rally Sputters: Markets Wrap
articles.title_zh: Stocks Fall as Nvidia’s Earnings Rally Sputters: Markets Wrap
articles.content_orig:
U.S. equities tumbled on Tuesday, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite hitting its lowest level in roughly seven months, as traders sold off semiconductor names ahead of Nvidia's much-anticipated earnings report.
Reports of a National Security Agency network outage added to recent jitters about the stability of the country's technology infrastructure and helped weigh on the market, traders said.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 848.75 points, or 1.64%, to end at 50,759.42. It dropped more than 1,000 points at its session low. The S&P 500 fell 1.03% to 7,340.53, for its lowest closing level since late July. The broad market index sank as low as 1.7% earlier in the session.
The Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.74%. At one point during Tuesday's session, it sank by as much as roughly 2.1% to touch its lowest level since April.
Major averages fell to their lows of the day following the report from CNN that said a classified network used by the spy agency had gone down, citing six people familiar with the matter. CNN's sources said there was no evidence that it was a cyberattack.
The NSA later in the day put out a statement saying the agency "experienced temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance." The agency added that "mission-critical capabilities remain fully operational."
Traders said the report helped take equities lower, though the losses were contained. This outage is latest in a string of incidents that have left people on edge including the FAA ground stop over the weekend, Microsoft's Outlook outage last week and some recent issues with banking apps.
Nvidia shares ended the session 0.5% lower amid investors' handwringing ahead of the company's earnings report due after the closing bell. However, the stock got a short-lived boost earlier in the session after Jensen Huang said he would be open to returning as CEO if the company's board thought that was in the best interest of shareholders.
"Nvidia should report strong results and guidance, but [it] is unlikely to be able to give investors solid answers to the questions heavily weighing on the stock [regarding] leadership and investigations around export controls," Ross Mayfield, investment strategist at Baird, told CNBC. "Strong demand might stabilize things, but the next leg higher will need some clarification around the 2028 and beyond outlook."
Other tech players ended the day in negative territory but well off their session lows, with Micron Technology sliding 0.9%. Advanced Micro Devices slipped 0.2%, while Intel was down 0.5%.
Microsoft shares were down 2%.
Neocloud stock Iren shed more than 3%. Nebius lost 1%. Investor Steve Eisman told CNBC earlier in the day that these stocks were among the names with the most to lose if the Huang scandal causes Nvidia to pull back its financing of the AI ecosystem.
U.S. equities closed lower on Tuesday.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed down 848.75 points, or 1.64%, lower at 50,759.42. It fell more than 1,000 points at its session low.
The S&P 500 shed 1.03% to end the session at 7,340.53, for its lowest closing level since late July. The broad market index sank as low as 1.73% earlier in the session.
The Nasdaq Composite was down 0.74% to 24,328.38 at the closing bell. At one point, it sank by as much as roughly 2.1% to hit its lowest level since April.
The VIX volatility index , a gauge of how much the S&P 500 might move in the next 30 days based on options trading, rose as much as 21% to an intraday high of 27.73, the highest since Nov. 6.
The VIX is now on track to rise for a fourth consecutive day for the first time since August 28.
Recent market volatility doesn't change UBS' conviction in the opportunity in artificial intelligence or its constructive view on diversified equities.
Investors weighing AI demand and the elevated capital expenditures from tech companies have sent stocks lower.
"Still, for the sell-off to indicate a lasting deterioration in the AI investment cycle, we would need to see weakening compute demand, slowing AI- related revenue growth, poor capacity utilization, or tighter financial conditions constraining spending by the largest technology platforms, Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi, chief investment officer for Americas, said in a note Tuesday.
Breadth of selling will also matter, and there is no evidence of that yet. Underlying demand for computing capacity also remains robust, he noted.
"We therefore continue to see potential for gains in broad equity markets over the next six to 12 months, supported by resilient economic growth and corporate earnings," Hoffmann-Burchardi wrote. "Near-term volatility reinforces the importance of selectivity and disciplined portfolio construction rather than a broadly defensive stance."
A CNN report Tuesday that a classified network used by the National Security Agency is down was just the latest to hit a stock market that's been battered lately by negative headlines. These include the FAA ground stop over the weekend, as well as Microsoft's Outlook outage last week.
"Any one of the stories that have have broken over the course of the last week or so would be enough to cause the market jitters. But when you compound that by having multiple stories — whether it's today's NSA report or the FAA ground halt or Microsoft Outlook being down for two days or Chase Bank ATMs not working — aggregate all of those, and it's easy for the human mind to get to a place where there must be something larger at play here," said Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth. "What's causing the market to have the kind of drawdowns that it's having today, it's just that aggregate of the compounding of bizarre stories that just have become too much of a headwind, at least in the near term," he added.
Investors may not be moved by Nvidia's upcoming earnings results, according to Megan Horneman, chief investment officer at Verdence Capital Advisors.
"I don't think there's going to be anything surprising from the earnings report," she told CNBC. "I don't know that we're even going to get much forward-looking information that people may be trying to get information on."
Horneman expects uncertainty to persist for the technology sector as investors assess what the trade could look like after "parts of Nvidia start to unwind."
"We're just stuck in this, I think, panic type of stage right now, and I don't know how far it will go," she said.
Another strong round of economic data, particularly on the consumer side, has led Goldman Sachs to take up its growth forecast.
The firm now sees  fourth quarter gross domestic product accelerating by a 2.4% annualized pace, up 0.6 percentage point from its prior outlook. Moreover, Goldman raised its backward-looking expectation for the third quarter, now looking for 3.8% growth from the period, which would be 0.4 percentage point higher than the advance estimate from the Commerce Department.
At the core of the more optimistic outlook is a retail sales report Tuesday that showed receipts up 0.2% in October — 0.6% when excluding autos and when focusing on the components that feed directly to GDP.
"The strength of today's report continues to reflect the resilience of the US consumer this year, as boosts from tax refunds and positive wealth effects from equity market gains have more than offset the drag from higher energy prices," Goldman chief economist Jan Hatzius said in a note.
Selling was broad across Wall Street midday Tuesday as declining stocks outnumbered advancers by nearly 3 to 1 on both the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq.
Declining volume accounted for roughly 69% of total NYSE volume and 71% on the Nasdaq, according to FactSet data.
On the NYSE, 1,924 stocks declined while only 700 rose. For Nasdaq, decliners totaled 3,036, compared with 1,141 advancers.
New lows also outpaced new highs. The NYSE recorded 362 new lows against just 20 new highs, while the Nasdaq logged 679 new lows versus 38 new highs.
— Deena Zaidi and Scott Schnipper

articles.title_orig: Mexico Leader Goes Viral in China for 21-Hour Economy Flight
articles.title_zh: Mexico Leader Goes Viral in China for 21-Hour Economy Flight
articles.content_orig:
President Claudia Sheinbaum promoted Mexico as an investment destination in an address to the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit in Shenzhen, China, on Tuesday.
In a 13-minute speech , she also touted Plan México — the federal government’s overarching economic and industrial policy — and spoke about a range of initiatives and achievements of her two-year-old administration.
Desde Shenzhen, China, les comparto mi participación en APEC CEO Summit 2026; en representación de México, expusimos a líderes económicos y empresarios del mundo que el desarrollo con bienestar es posible. https://t.co/3AEDA9Wve3
— Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo (@Claudiashein) November 17, 2026
According to a Xinhua news agency article posted to a Chinese government website , the APEC CEO Summit 2026 brings together “business and political leaders from across the Asia-Pacific and beyond to discuss regional economic cooperation and future development.”
“Under the theme ‘To Prosper and Win the Future Together,’ the two-day event has attracted more than 2,000 representatives from 21 APEC economies and 13 non-APEC economies, including Britain, France, Germany and Switzerland,” the article says.
“Participants include representatives from 115 Fortune Global 500 companies, as well as heads of several international organizations and representatives of business associations from Russia, the United States and other economies.”
In addition to speaking at the APEC CEO Summit, Sheinbaum will attend the APEC Leaders’ Meeting during her visit to Shenzhen. She arrived in the southern Chinese city on Monday and is scheduled to return to Mexico on Friday.
Promoting Mexico as a destination for foreign investment, Sheinbaum touted Mexican talent as well as the country’s geographic location and its trade agreements with other nations, among other competitive advantages.
“We have engineers. We are among the top five countries in the world in terms of the number of engineers produced. We have public universities, research centers, highly educated young people and a strong industrial tradition,” she said.
“We have the capacity to participate in major global value chains, but also to innovate and build strategic industries. We have a privileged geographic location, an extensive network of trade agreements, an economy integrated into the world’s major markets, natural resources, expanding infrastructure and, above all, the human talent of a hardworking people,” Sheinbaum said.
“Mexico guarantees conditions for investment, certainty and a long-term vision for development,” she said.
As part of Plan México, the federal government is seeking to attract more foreign investment to Mexico and strengthen and support the country’s vast manufacturing sector.
Foreign direct investment in Mexico reached a record high of almost US $35 billion in the first six months of 2026 , but the pace of year-over-year growth, at 2.1%, was not particularly strong.
By speaking at the APEC CEO Summit, Sheinbaum had the opportunity to court investment from major companies in APEC economies and beyond.
Three of Mexico’s five leading sources of foreign investment in the first half of 2026 are APEC members, namely the United States, Canada and Australia. Investment from China has increased in recent years , but the East Asian economic powerhouse was not among the top investors in Mexico last year .
Insecurity, uncertainty surrounding the future of the USMCA free trade pact — which the U.S. government has so far declined to extend to 2042 — and Mexico’s controversial judicial reform, which introduced the popular election of judges , are seen as among the factors discouraging investment in Mexico.
At the start of her address, Sheinbaum highlighted that Mexico is the world’s 11th most populous country and 13th largest economy.
“But above all, we are a nation with a history stretching back thousands of years, where Spanish is spoken, but so are 68 indigenous languages,” she said.
Sheinbaum went on to say that Mexico is building its “own” economic model with “roots in our history, our cultural greatness, and the strength, talent and capabilities of our people.”
“This transformation began in 2018. And starting in 2024, with the election of Mexico’s first female president, we gave it a new dimension through Plan México,” she said.
“Plan México is a vision for the nation. It is the decision to turn our capabilities, resources, strategic position, and talent into drivers of development grounded in sovereignty and social justice,” she said.
She said that the plan is based on “five principles,” namely “shared prosperity; energy and food sovereignty; public, private, and public-private investment in infrastructure; incentives for private investment; and environmental responsibility in the face of climate change.”
Sheinbaum also said that Plan México “has a humanist vision” in which “the economy is at the service of the people” rather than the other way around.
“For decades, it was argued that the wealth of a select few had to grow first, and that over time, the benefits would trickle down to the rest of society. In Mexico, we are proving that the path can be very different,” she said.
Sheinbaum said the government and private companies are expected to invest a total of US $432 billion in infrastructure under Plan México between 2024 and 2030.
“We are transforming the country’s productive capacity, connecting regions, bringing markets closer together, improving logistics, and creating jobs,” she said.
“At the same time, we are promoting investment in industry and services through incentives, certainty, streamlined administrative procedures, and new development hubs aligned with each region’s economic strengths. This has enabled us to become the fifth-largest economy in the world in terms of foreign direct investment,” Sheinbaum said.
In her closing remarks, she said she hadn’t traveled to China “just to offer investment opportunities.”
“We came to share a vision for the future,” she said.
“A vision in which Mexico grows and, at the same time, all economies become stronger and prosperity is a shared achievement,” Sheinbaum said.
In various ways, Sheinbaum’s address at the APEC CEO Summit was similar to her annual government report ( informe ) speeches, the most recent of which she delivered on Sept. 1 . The difference was that her speech in Shenzhen on Tuesday was delivered on the world stage and was directed at international businesspeople and leaders rather than a domestic audience.
In a vast auditorium in China’s tech capital, Sheinbaum acted as cheerleader in chief for Mexico, and also for the fourth transformation (4T) political project she leads. She highlighted that since Andrés Manuel López Obrador — the founder of the 4T — became president eight years ago, Mexico’s minimum wage has increased 154% in real terms and some 17 million people have been lifted out of poverty , according to World Bank data.
Sheinbaum also spoke about Mexico’s various social programs, and declared that her government is establishing a “ verdadero estado de bienestar ” — a phrase that can be read as a “true welfare state” or, more broadly, a country that prioritizes people’s well-being.
In addition, she highlighted her government’s major investment in highway, rail, electricity, water, port and housing projects.
Sheinbaum’s speech to the APEC CEO Summit came a day before Chinese President Xi Jinping is expected to address the event. Li Qingshuang , vice-chairperson of the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade, said on Sunday that leaders from 12 APEC economies, including Canada, Chile and South Korea, will attend the APEC CEO Summit and deliver speeches or remarks, or participate in panel discussions.

Diehard GameCube fans can connect the controller to their original console, or use it with the Switch.

If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
The 8BitDo 64 was a loose remake of the Nintendo 64’s unusual triple-grip controller that did away with that gamepad’s centered analog stick. But with its new GC Bluetooth Gamepad , 8BitDo has done a much better job at staying faithful to the design of the Nintendo GameCube’s excellent controllers, including their unique button layout, thumbstick design, and shoulder buttons.
The 8BitDo GC Bluetooth Gamepad is available for preorder starting today for $49.99 in orange or purple and is expected to start shipping on December 10th. That’s much cheaper than Nintendo’s $69.99 wireless remake of the GameCube controller, although 8BitDo’s version isn’t an exact copy of the original’s shape and ergonomics. If that’s important to you, and you have your GameCube’s original accessories on hand, you can still buy 8BitDo’s $25.98 upgrade kit, which is a cheaper way to make it compatible with modern consoles and devices.
8BitDo’s GameCube redux carries forward the original’s octagonal gates around the base of each thumbstick, making it well-suited to playing fighting games like Super Smash Bros. Ultimate . And while Nintendo continues to skip modern thumbstick technologies , the 8BitDo GC features both drift-resistant TMR thumbsticks and Hall effect linear triggers.
The controller connects to all versions of the Nintendo Switch over Bluetooth, as well as PCs or handheld consoles running Windows. It also comes with a 2.4GHz wireless USB receiver for players who prefer a connection with lower latency, or you can connect it with a USB-C cable for the best possible performance.

articles.title_orig: Shelly’s new smart valve shuts off your home’s water before a leak becomes a flood
articles.title_zh: Shelly’s new smart valve shuts off your home’s water before a leak becomes a flood
articles.content_orig:
The Neo Smart Water Valve works with Shelly’s sensors to stop a leak in about 12 seconds.﻿
The Neo Smart Water Valve works with Shelly’s sensors to stop a leak in about 12 seconds.﻿
If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
After releasing a $28 leak sensor earlier this year that conveniently runs off a battery for two years, Shelly is announcing an accompanying smart valve you can install on your home’s main water line to automatically turn off the flow when one of those sensors detects a problem. The Shelly Neo Smart Water Valve is available now through the company’s online store for $499.99, plus the cost of installation if you don’t trust your plumbing skills. It’s not a cheap solution, but it’s cheaper than the fallout of a leak turning into a disaster.
The Neo Smart Water Valve is designed to be installed on a standard US 1-inch thread connection (the company plans to launch additional size options next year) and is made from brass so it’s safe to use on plumbing carrying drinking water. It has an IPX7 waterproof rating so the valve will keep working if flooding means it ends up submerged. However, the valve lacks a battery of its own and requires a connection to a power source through an included USB adapter cable. Connecting it to a waterproof power bank instead of an outlet may be the best approach to ensure it still works during a power outage.
The smart valve connects to other devices over Wi-Fi or Bluetooth and is designed to integrate into existing smart home setups using webhooks, MQTT , or scripting for advanced users. In addition to shutting off the flow of water into your home in about 12 seconds, the valve also features an ultrasonic measurement system that tracks pressure, flow rate, your home’s consumption, and even the temperature of the water. Through the Shelly app, you can monitor all of that data in order to spot unusual usage patterns that could indicate a wasteful leak, or ensure the pressure doesn’t get high enough to damage pipes or appliances.

articles.title_orig: 8BitDo Reveals Its Own GameCube Controller For Switch 2
articles.title_zh: 8BitDo Reveals Its Own GameCube Controller For Switch 2
articles.content_orig:
8BitDo, known for its work in providing excellent retro-inspired controllers for modern systems, has announced the GC Bluetooth Gamepad to celebrate the GameCube's 25th anniversary. It's currently scheduled to launch on 10th December 2026 .
Compatible with Switch, Switch 2, and Windows, the GC controller maintains the core shape and layout of the iconic GameCube pad, but adds in a bunch of modern upgrades like TMR sticks and Hall Effect triggers. Priced at $49.99 , it undercuts Nintendo's official offering by $20 and is available for pre-order now.
Colours include purple and orange, which are arguably the most recognisable from the original release (though we're hoping for a Wavebird-inspired silver variant in the future, too). The pad also features single-rotor rumble to replicate the feel of the original, while a new 'ZL' button – which also features on the official Nintendo GameCube pad for Switch 2 – has been designed to be symmetrical to the 'Z' button on the right.
While we do have a dedicated capture button, there unfortunately doesn't appear to be a 'C' button for chat purposes. It's also not clear at this stage whether the GC controller will have wake-up support for Switch 2, but 8BitDo has generally been pretty good at including this, even if it's not necessarily supported immediately at launch.
Here's an official list of features from 8BitDo:
- Classic GC design and iconic button layout - TMR joysticks with octagonal gates - Hall Effect linear triggers - Single-rotor rumble - Symmetrical Z and ZL bumpers - Capture button for screenshots and recording - Turbo function - Support for multiple simultaneous gamepad connections
Finally, it's worth noting that if you purchase the 8BitDo Retro Receiver for GC , you can use the new controller – or indeed the official GameCube pad – with original hardware.

articles.title_orig: After years of waiting, Samsung finally brings native app lock to Galaxy phones
articles.title_zh: After years of waiting, Samsung finally brings native app lock to Galaxy phones
articles.content_orig:
Last updated: November 18th, 2026 at 16:55 UTC+01:00
SamMobile has affiliate and sponsored partnerships, we may earn a commission .
App lock is one of the new features introduced with the One UI 9.5 update.
Abhijeet Mishra / SamMobile
One UI 9.5 app lock feature
A feature that Galaxy fans have been requesting for ages has finally arrived. Samsung has introduced app lock with One UI 9.5 , giving users the ability to lock individual apps behind biometric authentication.
On previous versions of One UI, Galaxy users had to use Samsung's Secure Folder feature if they wanted to keep some apps and their data from being accessible to anyone using their phones.
However, Secure Folder doesn't just lock an app from being accessible to others. It also isolates apps inside Secure Folder from accessing the rest of the main system.
Because it creates an entirely separate, duplicate copy of an app, users are stuck managing separate logins, navigating into a separate vault, and dealing with restricted file and photo sharing with their primary phone profile.
Native app lock removes all that extra friction. Instead of locking your apps away in a digital safe, it simply puts a biometric guard on the apps you use every day. Even if you hand your unlocked phone to someone else, you can keep them out of your sensitive apps and data.
Abhijeet Mishra / SamMobile
One UI 9.5 app lock feature
Abhijeet Mishra / SamMobile
One UI 9.5 app lock feature
One UI 9.5's app lock works as you would expect: opening a locked app requires biometric authentication or your PIN, pattern, or password. Notifications from locked apps are hidden, and locking an app also removes its widgets from the home screen.
On the Galaxy S26 Ultra, app lock also works with Privacy Display: users can have Privacy Display turn on automatically every time they open a locked app.
The feature will likely be available on all Galaxy devices that receive One UI 9.5, but Galaxy S26 users are getting it first through the beta program Samsung launched on November 18.
Samsung will eventually expand the beta program to more devices before releasing the stable version of One UI 9.5 in 2027.
First Samsung device: SGH-D500
Abhijeet's writing career started with guides for custom firmware for Samsung devices (including the original Galaxy S), and he moved to SamMobile in mid-2013 and worked up the ranks to Editor-in-chief. In addition to phones and mobile devices, his interests include gaming on both PC and console, PC hardware, and spending countless hours on YouTube watching videos on tech, movies, games, politics, and internet dramas.

articles.title_orig: Ukraine Hits 2 Major Russian Refineries Again as Fuel Shortages Spread Across at Least 8 Regions
articles.title_zh: Ukraine Hits 2 Major Russian Refineries Again as Fuel Shortages Spread Across at Least 8 Regions
articles.content_orig:
In brief: Ukraine reportedly struck the Afipsky and Ilsky oil refineries in Russia’s Krasnodar Territory for the second time this month. The wider campaign has cut Russian crude processing by 30% and contributed to gasoline shortages and sales restrictions in at least eight regions.
Ukraine attacked two major oil refineries in Russia’s Krasnodar Territory overnight on Wednesday, Nov. 18, marking the second strike on both facilities this month, according to Ukrainian monitoring channels and Russian media reports.
A large-scale drone attack targeted the Seversky District of the Krasnodar Territory.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Debris from the drones sparked fires at two industrial facilities, while fragments were found at nine other locations, including private residential yards and streets, the region’s operational headquarters reported. Four people were injured and are receiving medical attention.
The Ukrainian monitoring channel Exilenova+ identified the facilities as the Afipsky and Ilsky oil refineries. Sources cited by the Russian independent outlet Astra also confirmed fires at both sites.
The Afipsky refinery is one of the three largest in the Krasnodar Territory and among the five largest in southern Russia. It can process more than 7 million tons of crude oil annually, producing gasoline, diesel fuel, jet fuel, and other petroleum products. The facility is focused exclusively on exports.
The Wednesday strike was the eighth attack on the Afipsky refinery since the beginning of the year and the second this month. It was last targeted by Ukrainian drones on Nov. 6.
The Ilsky refinery is also among the three largest in the Krasnodar Territory, with an annual crude oil processing capacity of approximately 6.6 million tons. It produces gasoline, diesel, and other petroleum products.
The facility was last targeted on Monday, when, according to Ukraine’s General Staff, three atmospheric crude distillation units were hit.
The Russian defense ministry said its air defense forces intercepted and destroyed 184 Ukrainian fixed-wing drones between 8 p.m. Moscow time on Tuesday and 8 a.m. on Wednesday.
According to the ministry, the drones were intercepted over the Belgorod and Rostov regions, Krasnodar Krai, Crimea, and the Sea of Azov.
Ukraine’s General Staff later confirmed that two oil refineries had been struck.
“Ukraine’s Defense Forces launched an aerial attack on the Ilsky and Afipsky oil refineries – two key fuel suppliers in southern Russia,” the General Staff said in a statement published on Telegram.
As per the report, explosions and smoke were observed near the Ilsky refinery, where storage tanks were hit.
Preliminary information indicates that an oil processing unit was struck at the Afipsky refinery. The facility has an annual processing capacity of 6.25 million tons, accounting for more than 2% of Russia’s total oil refining capacity.
The General Staff said the two refineries have a combined annual processing capacity of approximately 13 million tons of oil.
“Located in the south, they serve as the shortest supply route for fuel to Russian forces at the front. Therefore, every fire at these facilities means less diesel and gasoline for the Russian army, and fewer ‘oil-rubles’ – funds the Russian aggressor uses to purchase missiles and Shahed drones,” the statement said.
“Exercising their right to self-defense, as guaranteed by Article 51 of the UN Charter, Ukraine’s Defense Forces continue to take systematic measures to compel Russia to cease its armed aggression against Ukraine,” it added.
Kyiv resumed its campaign against Russian oil refineries in late October. Over the past few weeks, Ukrainian forces have struck around 10 of Russia’s 35 refineries, including facilities in Novokuibyshevsk, Ryazan, Afipsky, Saratov, Yaroslavl, Omsk, Nizhny Novgorod, Ufa, and Kirishi.
The attacks have contributed to a sharp decline in Russia’s oil refining volumes. Refineries were processing approximately 700,000 metric tons (5 million barrels) of crude oil per day at the end of October, but that figure had fallen to around 500,000 tons per day by mid-November – a reduction of about 30%, according to informed sources cited by Reuters.
The drop in refining capacity has also contributed to fuel shortages at gas stations in at least eight Russian regions, The Moscow Times reported .
Restrictions on gasoline sales have been introduced in the Leningrad, Nizhny Novgorod, Arkhangelsk, Novosibirsk, and Penza regions, as well as in the republics of Karelia and Buryatia.
In Moscow, Rosneft gas stations have reinstated purchase limits: Motorists can buy no more than 50 liters (13 gallons) of fuel per vehicle, while sales in canisters are capped at 20 liters.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

articles.title_orig: I watched Trump, Xi and Putin gather in China. Here are my top takeaways
articles.title_zh: I watched Trump, Xi and Putin gather in China. Here are my top takeaways
articles.content_orig:
SHENZHEN, China — It took a trip to China for me, an American, to see U.S. President Donald Trump in person for the first time.
Trump emerged from a group of black-clad photographers and other personnel surrounding him at a welcome banquet in Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Leaders' Meeting held November 17th to 19th.
Seated just a few spots to his left was Russian President Vladimir Putin who picked up a glass of red wine to join a toast led by Chinese President Xi Jinping .
"At tomorrow's Leaders' Meeting, we will discuss measures to expand mutual opening up, explore pathways to innovation-driven growth, and identify opportunities to expand practical cooperation across various fields, so as to translate more initiatives into tangible results," Xi said in Mandarin, according to a CNBC translation.
Xi was speaking broadly, but Thursday's agenda includes a bilateral meeting with Trump, and their highly anticipated trilateral meeting with Putin.
But looking at the mood in the room, it seemed that their trilateral conversation had already started Wednesday night at their long banquet table. Much of what happens at APEC, including bilateral meetings and other exchanges between leaders, takes place away from the media.
But what struck me was how little sign there was of the tension surrounding Nvidia 's CEO Jensen Huang resignation, a controversy that has gripped markets for the past 10 days.
Ahead of Trump's entrance into the banquet hall, Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao shared a friendly moment with U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and other members of the American delegation.
Last week, the U.S. officials said that Trump did not plan to raise allegations of Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy during his meeting with Xi.
It was a striking contrast to just two months ago, when I saw photographs of Huang and Tesla CEO Elon Musk sharing a table with Trump and Xi in Washington, D.C.
And when Trump visited Beijing in May, Huang took a few minutes to speak with reporters, including me, inside the Great Hall of the People. Musk was there too, accompanied by one of his sons.
This time, neither were visible in a room that was closely watched by the world. Musk was expected to join Trump's delegation in Shenzhen, but I did not see him Wednesday evening.
Their absence from the government-heavy banquet was striking. The world's most powerful leaders may be grappling with the implications of artificial intelligence, but they certainly didn't need the industry's biggest names at the table to do so.
China's Xi calls for removing trade and investment barriers
Putin says EU is losing industry, falling behind competition
Three things to watch as Trump, Xi and Putin meet in China
Over the months I've spent following APEC's "China Year," one thing has become clear: The forum has given Beijing an opportunity to host the U.S., Japan and other member economies at a time when unresolved tensions might otherwise have made such gatherings difficult.
But even in a year defined by talks of U.S.-China "strategic stability," the APEC events have exposed the rifts and the shifting dynamics in global power. Those dynamics were on display for the opening of the APEC CEO Summit.
Several hundred attendees, from Xiaomi CEO Lei Jun to U.S. Ambassador to China David Perdue, arrived early for the opening of the APEC CEO Summit.
After waiting in silence for at least 10 minutes, the audience welcomed Xi in a distinctly modern way: by raising their smartphones to capture the moment. The applause was rather muted.
It was much the same at the more government-heavy welcome banquet that evening. So many attendees rushed to take their own photographs of Xi and other leaders entering the room that reporters' views were largely blocked.
Following Xi's morning speech, there was a lengthy intermission before Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim took the stage.
"The entire multilateral framework needs to change," he said, praising China on its "rare" recognition of smaller countries.
During the tea break that followed, attendees quickly resumed mingling. Some even brought coffee and snacks back into the room as Putin prepared to speak.
They listened as the Russian president talked about his country's economic resilience and claimed Europe was losing ground. As attendees headed to lunch, one thing stood out: Neither Trump nor any other G7 leader had taken the stage at the opening event. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney spoke later in the afternoon.
The most visible American presence during the morning session came from business leaders appearing in a promotional video ahead of Xi's speech.
And the absence of an American voice was perhaps even more noticeable at Wednesday evening's banquet.
Trump did not follow Xi with a toast of his own. This was the same famously outspoken president, who in a winding speech in Davos, had declared that the U.S. must get Greenland .
Yet on Wednesday night in China, Trump wasn't the one holding the microphone.

articles.title_orig: Anthropic IPO: AI lab considers increasing the offering as investor demand surges
articles.title_zh: Anthropic IPO: AI lab considers increasing the offering as investor demand surges
articles.content_orig:
Anthropic is considering upsizing its initial public offering, people familiar with the details told CNBC, as the artificial intelligence lab weighs setting the price well above $80.
The company closed its order books and locked in total demand on Tuesday, setting the stage for the Claude creator's eagerly awaited Nasdaq listing. Institutional demand for the offering is around $400 billion, while retail demand is approaching $100 billion, according to the people, who asked not to be named because they were not authorized to speak publicly.
The orders are indications of interest and are not binding. All of the details are subject to change, and Anthropic will make final decisions Wednesday afternoon, the people said. Anthropic is expected to set its final IPO price after market close Wednesday.
Demand for the offering is higher than it was for Elon Musk's SpaceX , even though the rocket maker had a bigger market offering. SpaceX debuted on the Nasdaq in June in by far the biggest IPO on record, ultimately raising $85.7 billion.
The AI lab said last week that it would offer 825 million shares in the IPO at a price range of between $70 and $78 per share, which would net up to $64.35 billion at the high end of that range.
A representative for Anthropic declined to comment.
Anthropic's listing is a major test for the AI industry, which has experienced a set of recent shocks, including a dramatic backlash that was felt at the polls in the midterm elections and last week's ouster of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang . The market was already jittery on concerns that rising interest rates will make debt unaffordable for many data center developers and neoclouds.
Tech's biggest companies have significant exposure to Anthropic, as an investor, partner or customer. Amazon and Google both own stakes valued at over $100 billion, and a group of tech companies, including Google, Microsoft , Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices agreed to collectively invest $26 billion in the IPO. Anthropic, meanwhile, is a buyer of costly systems from Nvidia, Google, Amazon and AMD.
"I think if we do this right, we can create an age of miracles where humanity is able to solve problems that have eluded us for millennia," Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said in Anthropic's roadshow video . "We have to make sure that all the risks, all the ways that things can go wrong with this technology, we very carefully address those risks as we bring the benefits and as we have a viable business at the same time."
Amodei co-founded Anthropic alongside a handful of other researchers less than six years ago, after the group collectively defected from OpenAI. The company is best known for developing a family of AI models called Claude , and it primarily sells its products and services to other businesses.
Anthropic has been racing to maintain an edge over OpenAI and Google in the enterprise market, and it experienced a period of explosive growth in 2026, driven largely by the popularity of its AI coding tool, Claude Code. OpenAI has confidentially filed for an IPO and has said a debut is likely in 2027.
For the nine months ended Sept. 30, Anthropic said, it generated $33.24 billion in revenue, up roughly 1,200% from the same period last year, according to its prospectus. The company reported a $104 billion net loss during the nine-month period, though most of that was due to the change in fair value of convertible notes and derivative liabilities. Anthropic lost $25.1 billion over the same stretch in 2025, the filing said.
Anthropic said in an amended filing that its run-rate revenue was roughly $81 billion at the end of October, up $10 billion from the previous month.
The company has faced plenty of challenges during its meteoric rise over its positions on safety, regulation and national security, leading to two high-profile disputes with the U.S. government this year. Its prospectus included more than 90 pages of risk factors for investors to consider ahead of its IPO.
"Our aim is to help humankind chart a safe course through this technological evolution, open new frontiers of discovery, and bring forth an age of miracles," Anthropic's co-founders wrote in the company's prospectus. "Everyone who owns our stock, whether an institution or an individual, becomes part of that effort."

articles.title_orig: Designers’ notes: The Doom of Lord Carrard lore
articles.title_zh: Designers’ notes: The Doom of Lord Carrard lore
articles.content_orig:
Designers’ notes: The Doom of Lord Carrard lore
The latest Arcane Journal, The Doom of Lord Carrard , will be available to pre-order this weekend. To find out more, we undertook our own quest into the depths of the Warhammer studio to speak to the designers about the lore of the latest supplement.
JTY: Since the release of Warhammer: The Old World, we’ve been following the events of Settra the Imperishable’s war against the Old World. We’ve seen his armies advance through the Border Princes and navigate the peaks and valleys of the Vaults en route to the borders of Bretonnia. We’ve even seen what happens when an ancient Liche Priest leads an army of the Undead into the depths of Athel Loren . But what we haven’t covered in much detail is what caused all this turmoil in the first place.
In Arcane Journal – the Doom of Lord Carrard we decided to address this. We wanted to explore the charnel realm of Nehekhara in greater detail, and we felt Lord Carrard’s quest allowed us to do just that.
Much of the narrative is told from the perspective of the Bretonnians, giving us a relatable lens through which to view the horrors of the Land of the Dead. This allowed us to introduce Lord Carrard himself, a baron from the realm of Brionne, and establish his relationship with Sir Lothar of Kasos Rock, once a noble knight of Carrard’s court but now an outcast dwelling in the Border Princes .
It is the arrival of a messenger from Sir Lothar that sets in motion the events that are to follow. Bringing the grim forebodings from Sir Lothar’s court, the messenger warns of a great evil stirring in the Land of the Dead and implores Lord Carrard for his aid in vanquishing it. Rather than muster armies on the strength of vague portents, the baron elects to undertake a quest, riding in the company of his closest companions to the court of his former friend.
The next part of the story is told through the recollections of Sir Varo, one of the few to return and bring word of Lord Carrard’s fate, and of the evil that has been awakened in the Land of the Dead. Through Varo we learn of the Bretonnians’ journey to the accursed city of Zandri, from where we explore Nehekhara itself, coming face to face with the horrors of the Land of the Dead as the bold knights cross the deserts and battle the undead horrors placed before them. Accompanied by a wealth of stunning new art, this tale casts a whole new light upon this accursed realm, giving the reader a sense of the scale of the civilisation that once ruled the deserts of the Great Land, and the horrors a traveller might encounter in deserts haunted by looming horrors beneath skies shrouded behind impregnable dust storms.
But that’s not all. Arcane Journal – The Doom of Lord Carrard also examines ancient Nehekhara, in particular the major cities of that once-vibrant land, and the royal dynasties that once ruled over them. Delving into such ancient history was a fun challenge, and reading about the cities and dynasties of the Land of the Dead will hopefully inspire readers. There are lots of ideas here for theming your own collections of Tomb Kings of Khemri to reflect the armies of a particular city or monarch.
It’s always fun to explore the World of Legend, and shining a light on the events that led to Settra's climactic invasion was especially enjoyable. This was a story we were keen to tell, and we can’t wait to see how it will inspire readers!
Thanks, JTY! The new Arcane Journal is available for pre-order from Saturday, along with a wealth of reinforcements for the Tomb Kings of Khemri in the form of Skeleton Warriors , Skeleton Archers, Horsemen and Horse Archers , and Skeleton Chariots. Join us later in the week when we’ll be learning more about the rules in the Arcane Journal.

articles.content_orig:

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
The European Commission has proposed a new €45 billion ( approximately £37.5 billion) loan to help Ukraine as Russia intensifies attacks on critical infrastructure.
Ukraine anticipates a €70 billion (£58.3 billion) funding gap for 2027 as the war nears its fifth year.
Ursula von der Leyen , the bloc’s president, said Ukraine would only need to repay the loan after Russia had paid reparations for damage caused by the war.
The planned measure, which still needs approval from member states, would come on top of a similar loan of €90 billion (£75 billion) that was agreed by EU leaders at the end of 2026 to fund Ukraine.
Von der Leyen told reporters in Brussels that Europe “stands united” amid Russia’s war of aggression, reiterating the bloc’s support for Ukraine “in war and in peace”.
She added that Kyiv 's other international partners will be expected to provide the rest of the money to fill next year's funding gap.
The Commission proposes that up to €25 billion (£20.8 billion) of the new loan could be spent on military aid while the remaining €20 billion (£16.6 billion) has been earmarked on general budget support.
To finance the loan, the Commission will borrow on behalf of the EU on international markets, officials said.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy welcomed ⁠the proposal, saying the loan would "cover a significant part" of the country's budget and defence needs for next year.
"We very much hope for the swift adoption of this decision by the European Parliament and the Council (of EU governments) and count on the support of all EU member states," he said on X (formerly Twitter).
European Economy Commissioner Valdis Dombrovskis said Ukraine needed additional support because Russia is intensifying attacks on critical infrastructure and disrupting trade, particularly by blocking Black ‌Sea export routes.
"For almost five years, Ukraine has stood guard against the Russian aggression that also threatens our citizens, our territory, and our way of life,” he said. “Our support gives Ukraine a crucial strategic partner.”
Von ⁠der Leyen said she was confident all EU members would back the new loan, ⁠even though three — Hungary, the Czech Republic and Slovakia — opted out of the last one.
She said even EU countries that did not favour giving military aid to Ukraine were still committed to supporting Kyiv more generally, so their support for the loan could be attributed to meeting civilian needs.

articles.title_orig: Costco sees surge in panic buying after string of tech outages, report says
articles.title_zh: Costco sees surge in panic buying after string of tech outages, report says
articles.content_orig:
A series of tech outages has consumers stocking up on emergency supplies.
Costco sales are seeing a lift because of it, according to research firm Mizuho.
In the final week of October, Mizuho estimates, Costco's U.S. comparable sales, excluding gasoline, rose 11% to 12%, up from the normal 6% to 7% the first three weeks in October. Costco reported an 8.1% increase for the month. The firm said the stronger pace is continuing through November, as 21 of the 26 high-ticket generators it tracked on Costco's website sold out as of Sunday night.
Shares of Costco were roughly flat-to-lower in Wednesday morning trading at around $1,107 apiece.
"Consumer anxiety following the Microsoft Outlook outage, the ground stoppage for all U.S. airline flights, and apocalyptic concerns flaring up across social media have all contributed to increased emergency prep sales at COST," Mizuho analyst David Bellinger said in a research note Monday. Bellinger will appear on CNBC's "The Exchange" during the 1 p.m. hour.
On Thursday, an outage occurred in Microsoft's Outlook and Teams, and on Friday the Federal Aviation Administration halted departures nationwide. On Monday, a software outage at JPMorgan Chase caused banking transaction delays, and a system outage delayed United Airlines flights. The National Security Agency said Tuesday that the spy agency's communication network went down temporarily.
The outages appear to come amid a rush to recover software vulnerabilities uncovered by AI tools, and officials are saying there's no reason for panic.
Still, on TikTok and other social media platforms, posts urging people to stock up on food and supplies are gaining significant traction.
Mizuho raised its price target on Costco to $1,150 from $1,100 and kept its buy-equivalent outperform rating. The firm said U.S. comparable sales could grow more than 10% in November.
Mizuho also sees Walmart 's Sam's Club benefiting from emergency preparedness sales as shoppers fill up their pantries, and for Home Depot and Lowe's as they buy home improvement emergency supplies.
At Costco, Mizuho will be watching whether the surge brought in new member sign-ups when the warehouse retailer reports its first quarter of fiscal 2027 on Dec. 10.

Happy Tuesday! Here’s your Tuesday Tech Drop, some of the past week’s top stories from the intersection of politics and technology.
According to a new report from Reuters, the value of President Donald Trump ’s meme coin has cratered to record lows ahead of a cryptocurrency gala this weekend at his South Florida estate. The report also says that interest in the president’s third such gala “has collapsed.”
Rep. Robert Garcia, a California Democrat who is primed to become chair of the House Oversight Committee in January, told MS NOW that looking at Trump’s crypto ventures — and investors who may have felt legitimately scammed — will be a priority for his committee.

My colleague Steve Benen wrote about recent reports on the timing and frequency with which Trump has traded Nvidia stock that raise even more questions.
High-stakes negotiations are underway at the United Nations as representatives gather this week to discuss potential regulations on lethal autonomous weapons.

Lauren Chen, a right-wing influencer who has been accused of being paid by the Russian government to peddle pro-Kremlin propaganda to American audiences, made a recent appearance at the president’s Mar-a-Lago property in Florida.

articles.content_orig:
In the space of just five years, Anthropic has gone from unknown start-up to tech giant, worth more than a trillion dollars.
The company behind the AI platform Claude was formed by seven people who left rival OpenAI in 2021 and, in a matter of hours, will become multi-billionaires - on paper at least.
Anthropic is floating the business on the US stock exchange and will sell its shares at between $70 - $78 each.
If they go for the highest price, the founders' shareholdings will be worth at least $18.5bn each.
So, who are these people, all in their thirties and forties, who are about to become incredibly wealthy?
In 2020, Dario Amodei was working for OpenAI, the firm that brought generative artificial intelligence to a mainstream audience, when it launched Chat-GPT.
He decided he wanted to do things his own way, and left, taking his sister Daniela, and five colleagues with him.
Amodei grew up in San Francisco, impressing school friends not just with his academic prowess but also his speed on the running track , and his preoccupation with philosophical and technological questions including the potential of machines to gain consciousness and human longevity.
Initially he studied physics at Princeton and Stanford. But following his father's death from hepatitis C, he switched to biology and biomedical sciences.
Amodei did stints at the Chinese tech giant Baidu and Google before joining OpenAI.
But he began to worry that some people within the company were putting profit before safety, prompting the decision to jump ship.
Now 43, he is Anthropic's chief executive, and the person who, in his sister's words, makes the company "ambitious".
Dario and Daniela Amodei, were close growing up and later shared a flat together in San Francisco with other friends. She followed him into OpenAI and joined him when he left to found Anthropic.
She and her brother have always genuinely liked each other, she says, but the only thing she ever did first, was when he followed her in becoming vegetarian.
Amodei studied English Literature at the University of California Santa Cruz, going on to work for Democrat representative Matt Cartwright.
She has also worked at financial services platform Stripe, where she was head of risk operations.
The 39-year-old is president of Anthropic, manages the executive team, and leads the firm's research, engineering, product, governance and commercial work.
Tom Brown, now 39, followed the Amodei siblings when they left to found their new venture.
He led GPT-3 engineering at OpenAI, and prior to that was at Google on its DeepMind project.
Brown established his entrepreneurial credentials co-founding an app called "Grouper" that helps set up drinks between groups of friends.
He has supported US President Donald Trump's stance on datacentres, arguing that they are "an enormous source of prosperity".
Now as chief compute officer at Anthropic he is responsible for how the company secures and uses its computing resources.
Jack Clark, is another arts graduate among the original start-up's founding members and the only one who is not from North America.
Originally from Brighton in the UK, he studied English Literature and Creative Writing at the University of East Anglia and became a technology journalist, writing for publications including ZDNet UK, The Register, and Bloomberg.
He was caught up in the excitement of artificial intelligence and joined OpenAI, where he worked initially in communications, later becoming its policy director.
Now, 37, Clark is head of public benefit at Anthropic. He also leads the Anthropic Institute, an AI think tank.
Jared Kaplan, 42, is chief science officer at Anthropic, and heads its technical research. He is also an associate professor at Johns Hopkins University in Baltimore.
He holds a PhD in physics from Harvard University.
His work on scaling laws - which describe mathematical patterns that show that bigger AI models trained on more data tend to be more consistent - has helped provide AI firms with a framework for predicting AI behaviour, according to Anthropic.
Chris Olah is described as "interpretability research lead" primarily focused on how AI models work with each other.
But according to the New York Times, Olah has spent much of the last year convening meetings with faith leaders from across the religious spectrum.
Described by the newspaper as "boyish" but with "the zeal of an evangelist" the 34-year-old is reportedly exploring the relationship between morality and AI.
He previously led interoperability research at OpenAI, and prior to that was a research scientist at Google Brain.
The Canadian left the University of Toronto early, but later secured a Thiel Fellowship of $100,000, which is a scholarship to help gifted people move into research without a degree.
Sam McCandlish, 36, takes less of a public-facing role than the other founders, but like them will own around 1.6% of the company after its shares go on sale. As a result he too will see his stake crystallise into a hugely valuable asset.
McCandlish is Anthropic's chief architect, and helps shape and implement the company's policy designed to mitigate the risks of AI. Prior to this he worked on safety at OpenAI.
He has a physics PhD from Stanford, and maths and physics degree from Brandeis University outside Boston.

articles.title_orig: GTA 6: PS5 vs PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X and Series S: Which Console Plays Best?
articles.title_zh: GTA 6: PS5 vs PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X and Series S: Which Console Plays Best?
articles.content_orig:
Grand Theft Auto 6 is here - and that means we can finally share the full details of how the game performs on each console platform: base PS5, PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X and Series S.
We've already covered GTA 6's visuals in detail , focusing on the top-end experience on PS5 Pro, but the game's performance and fidelity can vary significantly depending on your platform of choice. The PlayStation and Xbox releases use different upscalers, for example, while the PS5 Pro release adds extra ray tracing effects. The Series S version is perhaps the most interesting of all, as it has to cram an extraordinary visual burden onto the weakest current-gen hardware - and more or less pulls it off, despite some noticeable cutbacks.
This article compares the game on every platform based on over 100 hours of testing across all four versions by John and Oliver, focusing on image quality, visual features and performance.
First, let's touch on resolution. The game runs at 2560x1440 (1440p) resolution on PS5, PS5 Pro and Xbox Series X, with no immediate signs of dynamic resolution scaling.
On PS5 Pro, this is upscaled to 4K using PSSR, the Pro's bespoke AI temporal upscaler. PS5 and Xbox Series X instead get a spatial upscale to 4K using Rockstar's in-house TAA. The game therefore doesn't use temporal upscaling - such as QSSR on PS5 or FSR on Series X - and appears visually softer as a result. However, the decision does make sense .
The Series S is the odd one out here, with an internal resolution of 720p, temporally upscaled to approximately 1080p using FSR 4. From what we understand, this is the first shipping game on Series consoles to use the new upscaler .
All platforms target a 30fps frame-rate, a rarity for a current-gen game, but given the huge scale and intense simulation elements, the design makes sense . There's no option for a 40fps or 60fps mode on any platform.
As an aside, Xbox consoles can run the game in a 120Hz VRR container as an OS-level feature, which allows for a slightly smoother experience. PlayStation users don't have a 120Hz option, and while you can force VRR on, the system-level VRR only operates above 48fps and doesn't support low frame-rate compensation, so this does nothing in a 30fps title.
In terms of performance, the PS5 Pro offers the smoothest experience, with a consistent 30fps experience through around 75 hours of standard play in our testing. However, it is possible to experience short drops to a minimum of 24fps when destroying vehicles with the grenade launcher, but the frame-rate tends to recover quickly.
The base PS5 and Series X use the same 30fps target, but hold it a little more loosely, often flicking between 30fps and the high 20s during traversal, combat and other more challenging scenes. Returning to the same vehicle destruction hotspot, the frame-rate remains in the mid-30s while the carnage is unfolding, and only recovers when we leave the area. Again, it's possible for frame-rates to dip into the low 20s at the worst case.
Series S offers the loosest 30fps lock, with large portions of the game playing out at frame-rates from the mid to high 20s. Again, it's possible to depress the frame-rate to around 20fps with vehicular destruction. The other consoles do a credible job of hitting 30fps, but Series S often lies in a 25-30fps no-man's-land.
Note that, distinct from frame-rate, the game featured some animation update rate unsteadiness in pre-release footage (and our early testing on Xbox Series consoles). Thankfully, this long-standing RAGE engine issue seems to have been fixed in patches prior to launch, and animations now play out with consistent frame pacing.
Finally, input lag is similar to other Rockstar 30fps titles, like Red Dead Redemption 2. We measured around 180ms of end-to-end camera movement latency on Series X, including a wireless controller and around 10ms of display latency. This didn't seem to change substantially across 60Hz, 120Hz and 120Hz VRR. This is similar to RDR 2 and GTA 5 Enhanced, though input response is perceptually a bit better in GTA 6.
While all versions of the game - PS5, PS5 Pro, Series X, Series S - use ray-traced global illumination (RTGI) and ray-traced reflections, only the PS5 Pro version additionally supports ray-traced shadows. On other platforms, less consistent shadow maps are used, though these do support variable penumbra and have a high-resolution appearance.
Note that the RT reflections on all consoles are part of a hybrid approach, with screen-space reflections (SSR) layered in.
The Series S version is surprisingly feature-complete compared to the PS5 and Series X versions, supporting strand-based hair and the two RT effects, but it does come with some cutbacks. Most notably, lighting is lower precision overall and RT reflections are softer, lower-res and sometimes miss details. Shadows also appear visually degraded, with lower resolution shadowmaps and some absent cutscene self-shadows.
Additionally, driving at high speed through the game world results in more noticeable pop-in. Other minor downgrades include muddier textures at oblique angles, lower-res volumetric clouds, flatter water, lower-res hair and facial hair, and lower resolution depth of field effects.
Despite these necessary cutbacks, due to the Series S console's more limited memory and cut-down GPU, the overall visual feature set is still similar to Xbox Series X and PS5. Thankfully, the full-fat CPU and SSD on the Series S mean that the scale and scope of Leonida isn't affected.
It's worth bearing in mind that the nature of the game make it hard to nail down absolutely every change, especially as John played only on PS5 and PS5 Pro, while Oliver played only on Xbox Series X and Series S. We'll have more direct cross-platform comparisons in future content.
In terms of visual features and performance, the PS5 Pro version is the best option available, with solid frame-rates, 4K-like image quality and a noticeable visual upgrade thanks to ray-traced shadows. However, the game looks and plays well on base PS5 and Xbox Series X as well, despite occasional minor frame-rate drops during regular play and a softer 1440p image. The Series S version of the game is the hardest to recommend, with consistent frame-rate drops to the mid-20s, a 1080p output resolution and a long list of visual cutbacks, though the overall character of the game's visuals still shines through.

articles.title_orig: Bill Gurley says giving away AI is Google's 'No. 1' move against Anthropic
articles.title_zh: Bill Gurley says giving away AI is Google's 'No. 1' move against Anthropic
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Bill Gurley , the venture capitalist behind an early bet on Uber ( UBER ), has an idea for how Google could slow Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) down: Give the AI away.
Gurley, a general partner at Benchmark, told Deirdre Bosa Live on Monday that Alphabet's ( GOOGL ) Google should use free AI to keep Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) and OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) from pulling away. Anthropic prices its IPO Wednesday and begins trading Thursday under the ticker symbol ANT .
"If Google recognizes that Anthropic ... and OpenAI maybe are getting escape velocity away from them, it is the No. 1 thing they should go do ... bar none," he said.
Gurley calls it playing defense. Open-weight models, which anyone can download, run and change for free, keep one company from locking up a market. Google did it with Kubernetes "when they were worried about Amazon and AWS," he said, and with Android "when they were worried about Apple having a monopoly in phones."
The catch? "We're not seeing those actions from Google."
Free models already do most of the work. On OpenRouter, a marketplace developers use to reach hundreds of AI models, seven of the 10 most-used models last week came from Chinese labs and are free to download. DeepSeek's V4.1 Flash alone processed about 77 trillion tokens, the basic units of text that AI models read and write. That's more than the other nine combined.
Duolingo ( DUOL ) CEO Luis von Ahn told Yahoo Finance last week that open models cut the cost of each AI video call to less than a cent from about 30 cents. "The vast majority of our usage of AI will be in open-weight models pretty soon," he said.
The money flows the other way. Closed models handled 28% of OpenRouter's tokens in mid-September but collected 73% of the spending, according to its September report . Similarly, Apple's ( AAPL ) iPhone accounted for about a fifth of phones sold in the second quarter but generated nearly half of revenue, according to Counterpoint Research.
Price is a big reason. Anthropic lists Claude Opus 5.5, its most-used model, at about 27 times what DeepSeek charges for its own. And while 39 companies sell DeepSeek's model on OpenRouter, nobody sells Claude Opus for less than Anthropic does. As Gurley put it, "The marginal price is going to equal marginal cost."
Gurley also called Anthropic's choice to write off model training costs right away, rather than over years, "pretty amazing," adding, "it's still profitable, really high gross margin."
"Anthropic — just reading through the S-1 — I think it's the most impressive business I've ever reviewed," Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management, said on Yahoo Finance's Market Hang on Friday.
OpenRouter tracks developers, not the ChatGPT or Claude apps. And Android cut both ways. It protected Google, but Apple kept collecting.
Gurley's worry is Washington. He said Anthropic's lobbying effort is "probably unprecedented for a company of their age or size," and he sees it as a push for regulatory capture , meaning rules shaped by the companies they govern. In AI, that could mean rules that favor closed labs over open models.
He still gives Anthropic its due. "It is remarkable what they've done," he said. "I tip my hat to them. I just wish they weren't lobbying so hard."
Internal AI tools helped analyze interview transcripts, research, and draft this post. Humans reviewed, edited, and fact-checked this post before publication.
Jared Blikre is the global markets and data editor for Yahoo Finance. Follow him on X at @SPYJared or email him at jaredblikre@yahooinc.com .

articles.title_orig: Jensen Huang has agreed to appear before Senate banking committee, Chairman Scott says
articles.title_zh: Jensen Huang has agreed to appear before Senate banking committee, Chairman Scott says
articles.content_orig:
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has agreed to appear before the Senate Banking Committee, panel Chair Tim Scott , R-S.C., said on CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Wednesday.
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has also agreed to testify, Scott said. The agreements to appear voluntarily come as pressure builds on Capitol Hill to investigate Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy, which led to his ouster at the chipmaker he founded.
"They both have agreed," Scott said. "We will hopefully have this done before Christmas."
Huang reached an agreement on Tuesday with the chairmen of three House committees for a closed-door transcribed interview on Dec. 1 jointly before the three panels. Scott had asked Huang to appear publicly in the Senate.
A spokesperson for the banking committee did not immediately respond to questions about when Huang and Lutnick would testify. In initial letters to the pair, Scott requested Huang appear on Dec. 3 and Lutnick appear on Dec. 10.
Scott said the appearances will provide the committee with "more information about what they knew, when they knew it and why they didn't do something about it."
"Nvidia seemed to have fairly lax controls, and I want to know how much of the relationship with Alice [Huang] impacted Nvidia's unwillingness or inability, or frankly, just blindness to Megaspeed's providing access to China of the most advanced chipset," Scott said of Jensen Huang's testimony.
The outgoing banking committee chair also homed in on Lutnick, calling for answers as to why the commerce secretary did not act after being warned about Megaspeed — the Singaporean company where the alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang, was an executive. Nvidia sold its chips to Megaspeed, which U.S. investigators suspect of diverting them to China.
"They were warned as early as March of this year, several months ago, that Megaspeed should be on the 'entity list,'" Scott said, referring to a Commerce Department list of companies the U.S. views as national security risks. The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security "didn't do it, Howard didn't do it, we want to know why."
Lutnick and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent have been embroiled in an intra-administration battle as the fallout from the Huang affair grows. Bessent on CNBC on Friday appeared to blame Lutnick for a lack of action on Megaspeed.
"You will have to ask them about their internal processes," Bessent said, referring to Commerce and noting his department has long supported imposing restrictions on Megaspeed.
A spokesperson for Huang declined to comment on Scott's announcement that he has agreed to appear.
Huang's upcoming appearances are likely just the start of the embattled former CEO's problems on Capitol Hill. Democrats will take control of Congress in January and have demanded sweeping investigations into the affair and Huang's cozy relationship with President Donald Trump .
The House Energy and Commerce Committee asked interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress for a briefing no later than Dec. 2 on the company's chip exports and information about the relationship between Jensen Huang and Alice Huang. The panel also asked Lutnick and a top deputy to appear to discuss chip export controls. The Wall Street Journal first reported the letters to Kress and Lutnick, and a committee spokesperson confirmed the report to CNBC.
— Megan Cassella and Ashlee Trujillo contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: 10 Features That Surprised Me While Playing GTA 6 On Xbox Series X
articles.title_zh: 10 Features That Surprised Me While Playing GTA 6 On Xbox Series X
articles.content_orig:
Copies of GTA 6 are beginning to arrive, with one difference spotted between the Xbox and PlayStation versions.
Grand Theft Auto VI ’s November 19 launch is almost finally upon us, with copies of the game already in the hands of many.
Preloads for digital copies of the game began on November 10 after Rockstar Games shifted the date forwards due to the title’s enormous file size .
For those who opted for code-in-a-box copies, preloads open today, on November 12.
Those who have a code-in-a-box copy in hand have taken to social media to reveal that the box features a double-sided fold-up poster, which is a nice touch.
One side features Lucia, with GTA VI ’s key art appearing on the other; the Grand Theft Auto franchise’s classic art style is used.
What has now been realised, however, is that those with an Xbox code-in-a-box copy are getting a slight downgrade compared to their PlayStation counterparts.
X (formerly Twitter) user GameRiot took to the site to share that “the GTA VI poster is actually smaller on Xbox compared to PS5”.
You can see in the video clip below that we’re not talking a couple of milimetres here.
There is likely a very good reason for this, as GameRiot points out, and that’s all down to case sizing.
While PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S physical cases are similarly sized, it appears that the area for posters, booklets, and such like within the Xbox case is slightly smaller.
Therefore, GTA VI ’s poster has been made smaller to fit accordingly, rather than this being any form of intentional slight to Xbox users.
It may feel that way amid Rockstar Games and PlayStation’s ongoing “plays best” marketing campaign that favours Sony’s console.
What isn’t abundantly clear yet is whether this difference in poster sizing is worldwide or whether this is unique to where GameRiot is based in the UK.
Grand Theft Auto fans are definitely seeing the humour in this latest spot.
“Cancelled my pre-order, unplayable,” joked BanksniO.
“They taking plays best on PS5 too seriously,” added vce_bby.
It’s a shame that Jason doesn’t get the chance to shine on the poster, unless he’s going to pop up elsewhere.
GameRiot did confirm that the PS5’s poster is roughly A3 sized while Xbox’s is understandably somewhat below A3 which could make the Xbox version difficult to frame, if that’s something you’re interested in.
READ MORE: GTA 6's first player ratings surface early via PlayStation Store, oops
It’s definitely been a busy week for GTA VI with an endless stream of marketing continuing to rollout.
Rockstar Games announced GTA VI : The Festival , a once-in-a-lifetime launch party based in Miami, Florida, plus Metacritic and Fandom have revealed a contest where you could win up to $500 in Visa gift cards simply by predicting GTA VI ’s Metacritic score .
We’ve also had confirmation that GTA VI will only run at 30fps , including on the PlayStation 5 Pro - something that’s ruffled a few feathers.
If you haven’t preloaded your game already, you may want to this weekend. GTA VI will be here before you know it.
